236// Debug Logging for ShowDebugLogWindow(). This is designed for relatively rare events so please don't spam.
237#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_ERROR(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventError) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); else g.DebugLogSkippedErrors++; } while (0)
238#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_ACTIVEID(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventActiveId) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
239#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_FOCUS(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventFocus) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
240#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_POPUP(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventPopup) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
241#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_NAV(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventNav) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
242#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_SELECTION(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventSelection) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
243#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_CLIPPER(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventClipper) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
244#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_IO(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventIO) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
245#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_FONT(...) do { if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventFont) IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
246#define IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG_INPUTROUTING(...) do{if (g.DebugLogFlags & ImGuiDebugLogFlags_EventInputRouting)IMGUI_DEBUG_LOG(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)

304// Debug Tools
305// Use 'Metrics/Debugger->Tools->Item Picker' to break into the call-stack of a specific item.
306// This will call IM_DEBUG_BREAK() which you may redefine yourself. See https://github.com/scottt/debugbreak for more reference.
307#ifndef IM_DEBUG_BREAK
308#if defined (_MSC_VER)
309#define IM_DEBUG_BREAK() __debugbreak()
310#elif defined(__clang__)
311#define IM_DEBUG_BREAK() __builtin_debugtrap()
312#elif defined(__GNUC__) && (defined(__i386__) || defined(__x86_64__))
313#define IM_DEBUG_BREAK() __asm__ volatile("int3;nop")
314#elif defined(__GNUC__) && defined(__thumb__)
315#define IM_DEBUG_BREAK() __asm__ volatile(".inst 0xde01")
316#elif defined(__GNUC__) && defined(__arm__) && !defined(__thumb__)
317#define IM_DEBUG_BREAK() __asm__ volatile(".inst 0xe7f001f0")
318#else
319#define IM_DEBUG_BREAK() IM_ASSERT(0) // It is expected that you define IM_DEBUG_BREAK() into something that will break nicely in a debugger!
320#endif
321#endif // #ifndef IM_DEBUG_BREAK

373// Helpers: Bit manipulation
374static inline bool ImIsPowerOfTwo(int v) { return v != 0 && (v & (v - 1)) == 0; }
375static inline bool ImIsPowerOfTwo(ImU64 v) { return v != 0 && (v & (v - 1)) == 0; }
376static inline int ImUpperPowerOfTwo(int v) { v--; v |= v >> 1; v |= v >> 2; v |= v >> 4; v |= v >> 8; v |= v >> 16; v++; return v; }
377static inline unsigned int ImCountSetBits(unsigned int v) { unsigned int count = 0; while (v > 0) { v = v & (v - 1); count++; } return count; }

447IM_MSVC_RUNTIME_CHECKS_OFF
448// - Wrapper for standard libs functions. (Note that imgui_demo.cpp does _not_ use them to keep the code easy to copy)
449#ifndef IMGUI_DISABLE_DEFAULT_MATH_FUNCTIONS
450#define ImFabs(X) fabsf(X)
451#define ImSqrt(X) sqrtf(X)
452#define ImFmod(X, Y) fmodf((X), (Y))
453#define ImCos(X) cosf(X)
454#define ImSin(X) sinf(X)
455#define ImAcos(X) acosf(X)
456#define ImAtan2(Y, X) atan2f((Y), (X))
457#define ImAtof(STR) atof(STR)
458#define ImCeil(X) ceilf(X)
459static inline float ImPow(float x, float y) { return powf(x, y); } // DragBehaviorT/SliderBehaviorT uses ImPow with either float/double and need the precision
460static inline double ImPow(double x, double y) { return pow(x, y); }
461static inline float ImLog(float x) { return logf(x); } // DragBehaviorT/SliderBehaviorT uses ImLog with either float/double and need the precision
462static inline double ImLog(double x) { return log(x); }
463static inline int ImAbs(int x) { return x < 0 ? -x : x; }
464static inline float ImAbs(float x) { return fabsf(x); }
465static inline double ImAbs(double x) { return fabs(x); }
466static inline float ImSign(float x) { return (x < 0.0f) ? -1.0f : (x > 0.0f) ? 1.0f : 0.0f; } // Sign operator - returns -1, 0 or 1 based on sign of argument
467static inline double ImSign(double x) { return (x < 0.0) ? -1.0 : (x > 0.0) ? 1.0 : 0.0; }
468#ifdef IMGUI_ENABLE_SSE
469static inline float ImRsqrt(float x) { return _mm_cvtss_f32(_mm_rsqrt_ss(_mm_set_ss(x))); }
470#else
471static inline float ImRsqrt(float x) { return 1.0f / sqrtf(x); }
472#endif
473static inline double ImRsqrt(double x) { return 1.0 / sqrt(x); }
474#endif
475// - ImMin/ImMax/ImClamp/ImLerp/ImSwap are used by widgets which support variety of types: signed/unsigned int/long long float/double
476// (Exceptionally using templates here but we could also redefine them for those types)
477template<typename T> static inline T ImMin(T lhs, T rhs) { return lhs < rhs ? lhs : rhs; }
478template<typename T> static inline T ImMax(T lhs, T rhs) { return lhs >= rhs ? lhs : rhs; }
479template<typename T> static inline T ImClamp(T v, T mn, T mx) { return (v < mn) ? mn : (v > mx) ? mx : v; }
480template<typename T> static inline T ImLerp(T a, T b, float t) { return (T)(a + (b - a) * t); }
481template<typename T> static inline void ImSwap(T& a, T& b) { T tmp = a; a = b; b = tmp; }
482template<typename T> static inline T ImAddClampOverflow(T a, T b, T mn, T mx) { if (b < 0 && (a < mn - b)) return mn; if (b > 0 && (a > mx - b)) return mx; return a + b; }
483template<typename T> static inline T ImSubClampOverflow(T a, T b, T mn, T mx) { if (b > 0 && (a < mn + b)) return mn; if (b < 0 && (a > mx + b)) return mx; return a - b; }
484// - Misc maths helpers
485static inline ImVec2 ImMin(const ImVec2& lhs, const ImVec2& rhs) { return ImVec2(lhs.x < rhs.x ? lhs.x : rhs.x, lhs.y < rhs.y ? lhs.y : rhs.y); }
486static inline ImVec2 ImMax(const ImVec2& lhs, const ImVec2& rhs) { return ImVec2(lhs.x >= rhs.x ? lhs.x : rhs.x, lhs.y >= rhs.y ? lhs.y : rhs.y); }
487static inline ImVec2 ImClamp(const ImVec2& v, const ImVec2&mn, const ImVec2&mx) { return ImVec2((v.x < mn.x) ? mn.x : (v.x > mx.x) ? mx.x : v.x, (v.y < mn.y) ? mn.y : (v.y > mx.y) ? mx.y : v.y); }
488static inline ImVec2 ImLerp(const ImVec2& a, const ImVec2& b, float t) { return ImVec2(a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t, a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t); }
489static inline ImVec2 ImLerp(const ImVec2& a, const ImVec2& b, const ImVec2& t) { return ImVec2(a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t.x, a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t.y); }
490static inline ImVec4 ImLerp(const ImVec4& a, const ImVec4& b, float t) { return ImVec4(a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t, a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t, a.z + (b.z - a.z) * t, a.w + (b.w - a.w) * t); }
491static inline float ImSaturate(float f) { return (f < 0.0f) ? 0.0f : (f > 1.0f) ? 1.0f : f; }
492static inline float ImLengthSqr(const ImVec2& lhs) { return (lhs.x * lhs.x) + (lhs.y * lhs.y); }
493static inline float ImLengthSqr(const ImVec4& lhs) { return (lhs.x * lhs.x) + (lhs.y * lhs.y) + (lhs.z * lhs.z) + (lhs.w * lhs.w); }
494static inline float ImInvLength(const ImVec2& lhs, float fail_value) { float d = (lhs.x * lhs.x) + (lhs.y * lhs.y); if (d > 0.0f) return ImRsqrt(d); return fail_value; }
495static inline float ImTrunc(float f) { return (float)(int)(f); }
496static inline ImVec2 ImTrunc(const ImVec2& v) { return ImVec2((float)(int)(v.x), (float)(int)(v.y)); }
497static inline float ImFloor(float f) { return (float)((f >= 0 || (float)(int)f == f) ? (int)f : (int)f - 1); } // Decent replacement for floorf()
498static inline ImVec2 ImFloor(const ImVec2& v) { return ImVec2(ImFloor(v.x), ImFloor(v.y)); }
499static inline int ImModPositive(int a, int b) { return (a + b) % b; }
500static inline float ImDot(const ImVec2& a, const ImVec2& b) { return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y; }
501static inline ImVec2 ImRotate(const ImVec2& v, float cos_a, float sin_a) { return ImVec2(v.x * cos_a - v.y * sin_a, v.x * sin_a + v.y * cos_a); }
502static inline float ImLinearSweep(float current, float target, float speed) { if (current < target) return ImMin(current + speed, target); if (current > target) return ImMax(current - speed, target); return current; }
503static inline float ImLinearRemapClamp(float s0, float s1, float d0, float d1, float x) { return ImSaturate((x - s0) / (s1 - s0)) * (d1 - d0) + d0; }
504static inline ImVec2 ImMul(const ImVec2& lhs, const ImVec2& rhs) { return ImVec2(lhs.x * rhs.x, lhs.y * rhs.y); }
505static inline bool ImIsFloatAboveGuaranteedIntegerPrecision(float f) { return f <= -16777216 || f >= 16777216; }
506static inline float ImExponentialMovingAverage(float avg, float sample, int n) { avg -= avg / n; avg += sample / n; return avg; }
507IM_MSVC_RUNTIME_CHECKS_RESTORE

540// Helper: ImRect (2D axis aligned bounding-box)
541// NB: we can't rely on ImVec2 math operators being available here!
542struct IMGUI_API ImRect
543{
544 ImVec2 Min; // Upper-left
545 ImVec2 Max; // Lower-right
546
547 constexpr ImRect() : Min(0.0f, 0.0f), Max(0.0f, 0.0f) {}
548 constexpr ImRect(const ImVec2& min, const ImVec2& max) : Min(min), Max(max) {}
549 constexpr ImRect(const ImVec4& v) : Min(v.x, v.y), Max(v.z, v.w) {}
550 constexpr ImRect(float x1, float y1, float x2, float y2) : Min(x1, y1), Max(x2, y2) {}
551
552 ImVec2 GetCenter() const { return ImVec2((Min.x + Max.x) * 0.5f, (Min.y + Max.y) * 0.5f); }
553 ImVec2 GetSize() const { return ImVec2(Max.x - Min.x, Max.y - Min.y); }
554 float GetWidth() const { return Max.x - Min.x; }
555 float GetHeight() const { return Max.y - Min.y; }
556 float GetArea() const { return (Max.x - Min.x) * (Max.y - Min.y); }
557 ImVec2 GetTL() const { return Min; } // Top-left
558 ImVec2 GetTR() const { return ImVec2(Max.x, Min.y); } // Top-right
559 ImVec2 GetBL() const { return ImVec2(Min.x, Max.y); } // Bottom-left
560 ImVec2 GetBR() const { return Max; } // Bottom-right
561 bool Contains(const ImVec2& p) const { return p.x >= Min.x && p.y >= Min.y && p.x < Max.x && p.y < Max.y; }
562 bool Contains(const ImRect& r) const { return r.Min.x >= Min.x && r.Min.y >= Min.y && r.Max.x <= Max.x && r.Max.y <= Max.y; }
563 bool ContainsWithPad(const ImVec2& p, const ImVec2& pad) const { return p.x >= Min.x - pad.x && p.y >= Min.y - pad.y && p.x < Max.x + pad.x && p.y < Max.y + pad.y; }
564 bool Overlaps(const ImRect& r) const { return r.Min.y < Max.y && r.Max.y > Min.y && r.Min.x < Max.x && r.Max.x > Min.x; }
565 void Add(const ImVec2& p) { if (Min.x > p.x) Min.x = p.x; if (Min.y > p.y) Min.y = p.y; if (Max.x < p.x) Max.x = p.x; if (Max.y < p.y) Max.y = p.y; }
566 void Add(const ImRect& r) { if (Min.x > r.Min.x) Min.x = r.Min.x; if (Min.y > r.Min.y) Min.y = r.Min.y; if (Max.x < r.Max.x) Max.x = r.Max.x; if (Max.y < r.Max.y) Max.y = r.Max.y; }
567 void Expand(const float amount) { Min.x -= amount; Min.y -= amount; Max.x += amount; Max.y += amount; }
568 void Expand(const ImVec2& amount) { Min.x -= amount.x; Min.y -= amount.y; Max.x += amount.x; Max.y += amount.y; }
569 void Translate(const ImVec2& d) { Min.x += d.x; Min.y += d.y; Max.x += d.x; Max.y += d.y; }
570 void TranslateX(float dx) { Min.x += dx; Max.x += dx; }
571 void TranslateY(float dy) { Min.y += dy; Max.y += dy; }
572 void ClipWith(const ImRect& r) { Min = ImMax(Min, r.Min); Max = ImMin(Max, r.Max); } // Simple version, may lead to an inverted rectangle, which is fine for Contains/Overlaps test but not for display.
573 void ClipWithFull(const ImRect& r) { Min = ImClamp(Min, r.Min, r.Max); Max = ImClamp(Max, r.Min, r.Max); } // Full version, ensure both points are fully clipped.
574 void Floor() { Min.x = IM_TRUNC(Min.x); Min.y = IM_TRUNC(Min.y); Max.x = IM_TRUNC(Max.x); Max.y = IM_TRUNC(Max.y); }
575 bool IsInverted() const { return Min.x > Max.x || Min.y > Max.y; }
576 ImVec4 ToVec4() const { return ImVec4(Min.x, Min.y, Max.x, Max.y); }
577};

579// Helper: ImBitArray
580#define IM_BITARRAY_TESTBIT(_ARRAY, _N) ((_ARRAY[(_N) >> 5] & ((ImU32)1 << ((_N) & 31))) != 0) // Macro version of ImBitArrayTestBit(): ensure args have side-effect or are costly!
581#define IM_BITARRAY_CLEARBIT(_ARRAY, _N) ((_ARRAY[(_N) >> 5] &= ~((ImU32)1 << ((_N) & 31)))) // Macro version of ImBitArrayClearBit(): ensure args have side-effect or are costly!
582inline size_t ImBitArrayGetStorageSizeInBytes(int bitcount) { return (size_t)((bitcount + 31) >> 5) << 2; }
583inline void ImBitArrayClearAllBits(ImU32* arr, int bitcount){ memset(arr, 0, ImBitArrayGetStorageSizeInBytes(bitcount)); }
584inline bool ImBitArrayTestBit(const ImU32* arr, int n) { ImU32 mask = (ImU32)1 << (n & 31); return (arr[n >> 5] & mask) != 0; }
585inline void ImBitArrayClearBit(ImU32* arr, int n) { ImU32 mask = (ImU32)1 << (n & 31); arr[n >> 5] &= ~mask; }
586inline void ImBitArraySetBit(ImU32* arr, int n) { ImU32 mask = (ImU32)1 << (n & 31); arr[n >> 5] |= mask; }
587inline void ImBitArraySetBitRange(ImU32* arr, int n, int n2) // Works on range [n..n2)
588{
589 n2--;
590 while (n <= n2)
591 {
592 int a_mod = (n & 31);
593 int b_mod = (n2 > (n | 31) ? 31 : (n2 & 31)) + 1;
594 ImU32 mask = (ImU32)(((ImU64)1 << b_mod) - 1) & ~(ImU32)(((ImU64)1 << a_mod) - 1);
595 arr[n >> 5] |= mask;
596 n = (n + 32) & ~31;
597 }
598}
599
600typedef ImU32* ImBitArrayPtr; // Name for use in structs
601
602// Helper: ImBitArray class (wrapper over ImBitArray functions)
603// Store 1-bit per value.
604template<int BITCOUNT, int OFFSET = 0>
605struct ImBitArray
606{
607 ImU32 Storage[(BITCOUNT + 31) >> 5];
608 ImBitArray() { ClearAllBits(); }
609 void ClearAllBits() { memset(Storage, 0, sizeof(Storage)); }
610 void SetAllBits() { memset(Storage, 255, sizeof(Storage)); }
611 bool TestBit(int n) const { n += OFFSET; IM_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < BITCOUNT); return IM_BITARRAY_TESTBIT(Storage, n); }
612 void SetBit(int n) { n += OFFSET; IM_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < BITCOUNT); ImBitArraySetBit(Storage, n); }
613 void ClearBit(int n) { n += OFFSET; IM_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < BITCOUNT); ImBitArrayClearBit(Storage, n); }
614 void SetBitRange(int n, int n2) { n += OFFSET; n2 += OFFSET; IM_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < BITCOUNT && n2 > n && n2 <= BITCOUNT); ImBitArraySetBitRange(Storage, n, n2); } // Works on range [n..n2)
615 bool operator[](int n) const { n += OFFSET; IM_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < BITCOUNT); return IM_BITARRAY_TESTBIT(Storage, n); }
616};

618// Helper: ImBitVector
619// Store 1-bit per value.
620struct IMGUI_API ImBitVector
621{
622 ImVector<ImU32> Storage;
623 void Create(int sz) { Storage.resize((sz + 31) >> 5); memset(Storage.Data, 0, (size_t)Storage.Size * sizeof(Storage.Data[0])); }
624 void Clear() { Storage.clear(); }
625 bool TestBit(int n) const { IM_ASSERT(n < (Storage.Size << 5)); return IM_BITARRAY_TESTBIT(Storage.Data, n); }
626 void SetBit(int n) { IM_ASSERT(n < (Storage.Size << 5)); ImBitArraySetBit(Storage.Data, n); }
627 void ClearBit(int n) { IM_ASSERT(n < (Storage.Size << 5)); ImBitArrayClearBit(Storage.Data, n); }
628};

631// Helper: ImSpan<>
632// Pointing to a span of data we don't own.
633template<typename T>
634struct ImSpan
635{
636 T* Data;
637 T* DataEnd;
638
639 // Constructors, destructor
640 inline ImSpan() { Data = DataEnd = NULL; }
641 inline ImSpan(T* data, int size) { Data = data; DataEnd = data + size; }
642 inline ImSpan(T* data, T* data_end) { Data = data; DataEnd = data_end; }
643
644 inline void set(T* data, int size) { Data = data; DataEnd = data + size; }
645 inline void set(T* data, T* data_end) { Data = data; DataEnd = data_end; }
646 inline int size() const { return (int)(ptrdiff_t)(DataEnd - Data); }
647 inline int size_in_bytes() const { return (int)(ptrdiff_t)(DataEnd - Data) * (int)sizeof(T); }
648 inline T& operator[](int i) { T* p = Data + i; IM_ASSERT(p >= Data && p < DataEnd); return *p; }
649 inline const T& operator[](int i) const { const T* p = Data + i; IM_ASSERT(p >= Data && p < DataEnd); return *p; }
650
651 inline T* begin() { return Data; }
652 inline const T* begin() const { return Data; }
653 inline T* end() { return DataEnd; }
654 inline const T* end() const { return DataEnd; }
655
656 // Utilities
657 inline int index_from_ptr(const T* it) const { IM_ASSERT(it >= Data && it < DataEnd); const ptrdiff_t off = it - Data; return (int)off; }
658};

660// Helper: ImSpanAllocator<>
661// Facilitate storing multiple chunks into a single large block (the "arena")
662// - Usage: call Reserve() N times, allocate GetArenaSizeInBytes() worth, pass it to SetArenaBasePtr(), call GetSpan() N times to retrieve the aligned ranges.
663template<int CHUNKS>
664struct ImSpanAllocator
665{
666 char* BasePtr;
667 int CurrOff;
668 int CurrIdx;
669 int Offsets[CHUNKS];
670 int Sizes[CHUNKS];
671
672 ImSpanAllocator() { memset(this, 0, sizeof(*this)); }
673 inline void Reserve(int n, size_t sz, int a=4) { IM_ASSERT(n == CurrIdx && n < CHUNKS); CurrOff = IM_MEMALIGN(CurrOff, a); Offsets[n] = CurrOff; Sizes[n] = (int)sz; CurrIdx++; CurrOff += (int)sz; }
674 inline int GetArenaSizeInBytes() { return CurrOff; }
675 inline void SetArenaBasePtr(void* base_ptr) { BasePtr = (char*)base_ptr; }
676 inline void* GetSpanPtrBegin(int n) { IM_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < CHUNKS && CurrIdx == CHUNKS); return (void*)(BasePtr + Offsets[n]); }
677 inline void* GetSpanPtrEnd(int n) { IM_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < CHUNKS && CurrIdx == CHUNKS); return (void*)(BasePtr + Offsets[n] + Sizes[n]); }
678 template<typename T>
679 inline void GetSpan(int n, ImSpan<T>* span) { span->set((T*)GetSpanPtrBegin(n), (T*)GetSpanPtrEnd(n)); }
680};
681
682// Helper: ImPool<>
683// Basic keyed storage for contiguous instances, slow/amortized insertion, O(1) indexable, O(Log N) queries by ID over a dense/hot buffer,
684// Honor constructor/destructor. Add/remove invalidate all pointers. Indexes have the same lifetime as the associated object.
685typedef int ImPoolIdx;
686template<typename T>
687struct ImPool
688{
689 ImVector<T> Buf; // Contiguous data
690 ImGuiStorage Map; // ID->Index
691 ImPoolIdx FreeIdx; // Next free idx to use
692 ImPoolIdx AliveCount; // Number of active/alive items (for display purpose)
693
694 ImPool() { FreeIdx = AliveCount = 0; }
695 ~ImPool() { Clear(); }
696 T* GetByKey(ImGuiID key) { int idx = Map.GetInt(key, -1); return (idx != -1) ? &Buf[idx] : NULL; }
697 T* GetByIndex(ImPoolIdx n) { return &Buf[n]; }
698 ImPoolIdx GetIndex(const T* p) const { IM_ASSERT(p >= Buf.Data && p < Buf.Data + Buf.Size); return (ImPoolIdx)(p - Buf.Data); }
699 T* GetOrAddByKey(ImGuiID key) { int* p_idx = Map.GetIntRef(key, -1); if (*p_idx != -1) return &Buf[*p_idx]; *p_idx = FreeIdx; return Add(); }
700 bool Contains(const T* p) const { return (p >= Buf.Data && p < Buf.Data + Buf.Size); }
701 void Clear() { for (int n = 0; n < Map.Data.Size; n++) { int idx = Map.Data[n].val_i; if (idx != -1) Buf[idx].~T(); } Map.Clear(); Buf.clear(); FreeIdx = AliveCount = 0; }
702 T* Add() { int idx = FreeIdx; if (idx == Buf.Size) { Buf.resize(Buf.Size + 1); FreeIdx++; } else { FreeIdx = *(int*)&Buf[idx]; } IM_PLACEMENT_NEW(&Buf[idx]) T(); AliveCount++; return &Buf[idx]; }
703 void Remove(ImGuiID key, const T* p) { Remove(key, GetIndex(p)); }
704 void Remove(ImGuiID key, ImPoolIdx idx) { Buf[idx].~T(); *(int*)&Buf[idx] = FreeIdx; FreeIdx = idx; Map.SetInt(key, -1); AliveCount--; }
705 void Reserve(int capacity) { Buf.reserve(capacity); Map.Data.reserve(capacity); }
706
707 // To iterate a ImPool: for (int n = 0; n < pool.GetMapSize(); n++) if (T* t = pool.TryGetMapData(n)) { ... }
708 // Can be avoided if you know .Remove() has never been called on the pool, or AliveCount == GetMapSize()
709 int GetAliveCount() const { return AliveCount; } // Number of active/alive items in the pool (for display purpose)
710 int GetBufSize() const { return Buf.Size; }
711 int GetMapSize() const { return Map.Data.Size; } // It is the map we need iterate to find valid items, since we don't have "alive" storage anywhere
712 T* TryGetMapData(ImPoolIdx n) { int idx = Map.Data[n].val_i; if (idx == -1) return NULL; return GetByIndex(idx); }
713};
714
715// Helper: ImChunkStream<>
716// Build and iterate a contiguous stream of variable-sized structures.
717// This is used by Settings to store persistent data while reducing allocation count.
718// We store the chunk size first, and align the final size on 4 bytes boundaries.
719// The tedious/zealous amount of casting is to avoid -Wcast-align warnings.
720template<typename T>
721struct ImChunkStream
722{
723 ImVector<char> Buf;
724
725 void clear() { Buf.clear(); }
726 bool empty() const { return Buf.Size == 0; }
727 int size() const { return Buf.Size; }
728 T* alloc_chunk(size_t sz) { size_t HDR_SZ = 4; sz = IM_MEMALIGN(HDR_SZ + sz, 4u); int off = Buf.Size; Buf.resize(off + (int)sz); ((int*)(void*)(Buf.Data + off))[0] = (int)sz; return (T*)(void*)(Buf.Data + off + (int)HDR_SZ); }
729 T* begin() { size_t HDR_SZ = 4; if (!Buf.Data) return NULL; return (T*)(void*)(Buf.Data + HDR_SZ); }
730 T* next_chunk(T* p) { size_t HDR_SZ = 4; IM_ASSERT(p >= begin() && p < end()); p = (T*)(void*)((char*)(void*)p + chunk_size(p)); if (p == (T*)(void*)((char*)end() + HDR_SZ)) return (T*)0; IM_ASSERT(p < end()); return p; }
731 int chunk_size(const T* p) { return ((const int*)p)[-1]; }
732 T* end() { return (T*)(void*)(Buf.Data + Buf.Size); }
733 int offset_from_ptr(const T* p) { IM_ASSERT(p >= begin() && p < end()); const ptrdiff_t off = (const char*)p - Buf.Data; return (int)off; }
734 T* ptr_from_offset(int off) { IM_ASSERT(off >= 4 && off < Buf.Size); return (T*)(void*)(Buf.Data + off); }
735 void swap(ImChunkStream<T>& rhs) { rhs.Buf.swap(Buf); }
736};

738// Helper: ImGuiTextIndex
739// Maintain a line index for a text buffer. This is a strong candidate to be moved into the public API.
740struct ImGuiTextIndex
741{
742 ImVector<int> LineOffsets;
743 int EndOffset = 0; // Because we don't own text buffer we need to maintain EndOffset (may bake in LineOffsets?)
744
745 void clear() { LineOffsets.clear(); EndOffset = 0; }
746 int size() { return LineOffsets.Size; }
747 const char* get_line_begin(const char* base, int n) { return base + LineOffsets[n]; }
748 const char* get_line_end(const char* base, int n) { return base + (n + 1 < LineOffsets.Size ? (LineOffsets[n + 1] - 1) : EndOffset); }
749 void append(const char* base, int old_size, int new_size);
750};

755//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
756// [SECTION] ImDrawList support
757//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
758
759// ImDrawList: Helper function to calculate a circle's segment count given its radius and a "maximum error" value.
760// Estimation of number of circle segment based on error is derived using method described in https://stackoverflow.com/a/2244088/15194693
761// Number of segments (N) is calculated using equation:
762// N = ceil ( pi / acos(1 - error / r) ) where r > 0, error <= r
763// Our equation is significantly simpler that one in the post thanks for choosing segment that is
764// perpendicular to X axis. Follow steps in the article from this starting condition and you will
765// will get this result.
766//
767// Rendering circles with an odd number of segments, while mathematically correct will produce
768// asymmetrical results on the raster grid. Therefore we're rounding N to next even number (7->8, 8->8, 9->10 etc.)
769#define IM_ROUNDUP_TO_EVEN(_V) ((((_V) + 1) / 2) * 2)
770#define IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_MIN 4
771#define IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_MAX 512
772#define IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_CALC(_RAD,_MAXERROR) ImClamp(IM_ROUNDUP_TO_EVEN((int)ImCeil(IM_PI / ImAcos(1 - ImMin((_MAXERROR), (_RAD)) / (_RAD)))), IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_MIN, IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_MAX)
773
774// Raw equation from IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_CALC rewritten for 'r' and 'error'.
775#define IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_CALC_R(_N,_MAXERROR) ((_MAXERROR) / (1 - ImCos(IM_PI / ImMax((float)(_N), IM_PI))))
776#define IM_DRAWLIST_CIRCLE_AUTO_SEGMENT_CALC_ERROR(_N,_RAD) ((1 - ImCos(IM_PI / ImMax((float)(_N), IM_PI))) / (_RAD))
777
778// ImDrawList: Lookup table size for adaptive arc drawing, cover full circle.
779#ifndef IM_DRAWLIST_ARCFAST_TABLE_SIZE
780#define IM_DRAWLIST_ARCFAST_TABLE_SIZE 48 // Number of samples in lookup table.
781#endif
782#define IM_DRAWLIST_ARCFAST_SAMPLE_MAX IM_DRAWLIST_ARCFAST_TABLE_SIZE // Sample index _PathArcToFastEx() for 360 angle.
783
784// Data shared between all ImDrawList instances
785// Conceptually this could have been called e.g. ImDrawListSharedContext
786// Typically one ImGui context would create and maintain one of this.
787// You may want to create your own instance of you try to ImDrawList completely without ImGui. In that case, watch out for future changes to this structure.
788struct IMGUI_API ImDrawListSharedData
789{
790 ImVec2 TexUvWhitePixel; // UV of white pixel in the atlas
791 const ImVec4* TexUvLines; // UV of anti-aliased lines in the atlas
792 ImFont* Font; // Current/default font (optional, for simplified AddText overload)
793 float FontSize; // Current/default font size (optional, for simplified AddText overload)
794 float FontScale; // Current/default font scale (== FontSize / Font->FontSize)
795 float CurveTessellationTol; // Tessellation tolerance when using PathBezierCurveTo()
796 float CircleSegmentMaxError; // Number of circle segments to use per pixel of radius for AddCircle() etc
797 float InitialFringeScale; // Initial scale to apply to AA fringe
798 ImDrawListFlags InitialFlags; // Initial flags at the beginning of the frame (it is possible to alter flags on a per-drawlist basis afterwards)
799 ImVec4 ClipRectFullscreen; // Value for PushClipRectFullscreen()
800 ImVector<ImVec2> TempBuffer; // Temporary write buffer
801
802 // Lookup tables
803 ImVec2 ArcFastVtx[IM_DRAWLIST_ARCFAST_TABLE_SIZE]; // Sample points on the quarter of the circle.
804 float ArcFastRadiusCutoff; // Cutoff radius after which arc drawing will fallback to slower PathArcTo()
805 ImU8 CircleSegmentCounts[64]; // Precomputed segment count for given radius before we calculate it dynamically (to avoid calculation overhead)
806
807 ImDrawListSharedData();
808 void SetCircleTessellationMaxError(float max_error);
809};

1163 int ReloadSelectionEnd;

1463// Input function taking an 'ImGuiID owner_id' argument defaults to (ImGuiKeyOwner_Any == 0) aka don't test ownership, which matches legacy behavior.

1466//#define ImGuiKeyOwner_None ImGuiKeyOwner_NoOwner // We previously called this 'ImGuiKeyOwner_None' but it was inconsistent with our pattern that _None values == 0 and quite dangerous. Also using _NoOwner makes the IsKeyPressed() calls more explicit.

1478 ImGuiID RoutingNext;

1483// Routing table: maintain a desired owner for each possible key-chord (key + mods), and setup owner in NewFrame() when mods are matching.
1484// Stored in main context (1 instance)
1485struct ImGuiKeyRoutingTable
1486{
1487 ImGuiKeyRoutingIndex Index[ImGuiKey_NamedKey_COUNT]; // Index of first entry in Entries[]
1488 ImVector<ImGuiKeyRoutingData> Entries;
1489 ImVector<ImGuiKeyRoutingData> EntriesNext; // Double-buffer to avoid reallocation (could use a shared buffer)
1490
1491 ImGuiKeyRoutingTable() { Clear(); }
1492 void Clear() { for (int n = 0; n < IM_ARRAYSIZE(Index); n++) Index[n] = -1; Entries.clear(); EntriesNext.clear(); }
1493};

1502 bool LockUntilRelease; // Reading this key requires explicit owner id (until key is released). Set by ImGuiInputFlags_LockUntilRelease. When this is true LockThisFrame is always true as well.

1507// Extend ImGuiInputFlags_
1508// Flags for extended versions of IsKeyPressed(), IsMouseClicked(), Shortcut(), SetKeyOwner(), SetItemKeyOwner()
1509// Don't mistake with ImGuiInputTextFlags! (which is for ImGui::InputText() function)
1510enum ImGuiInputFlagsPrivate_
1511{
1512 // Flags for IsKeyPressed(), IsKeyChordPressed(), IsMouseClicked(), Shortcut()
1513 // - Repeat mode: Repeat rate selection
1514 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateDefault = 1 << 1, // Repeat rate: Regular (default)
1515 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateNavMove = 1 << 2, // Repeat rate: Fast
1516 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateNavTweak = 1 << 3, // Repeat rate: Faster
1517 // - Repeat mode: Specify when repeating key pressed can be interrupted.
1518 // - In theory ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilOtherKeyPress may be a desirable default, but it would break too many behavior so everything is opt-in.
1519 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilRelease = 1 << 4, // Stop repeating when released (default for all functions except Shortcut). This only exists to allow overriding Shortcut() default behavior.
1520 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilKeyModsChange = 1 << 5, // Stop repeating when released OR if keyboard mods are changed (default for Shortcut)
1521 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilKeyModsChangeFromNone = 1 << 6, // Stop repeating when released OR if keyboard mods are leaving the None state. Allows going from Mod+Key to Key by releasing Mod.
1522 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilOtherKeyPress = 1 << 7, // Stop repeating when released OR if any other keyboard key is pressed during the repeat
1523
1524 // Flags for SetKeyOwner(), SetItemKeyOwner()
1525 // - Locking key away from non-input aware code. Locking is useful to make input-owner-aware code steal keys from non-input-owner-aware code. If all code is input-owner-aware locking would never be necessary.
1526 ImGuiInputFlags_LockThisFrame = 1 << 20, // Further accesses to key data will require EXPLICIT owner ID (ImGuiKeyOwner_Any/0 will NOT accepted for polling). Cleared at end of frame.
1527 ImGuiInputFlags_LockUntilRelease = 1 << 21, // Further accesses to key data will require EXPLICIT owner ID (ImGuiKeyOwner_Any/0 will NOT accepted for polling). Cleared when the key is released or at end of each frame if key is released.
1528
1529 // - Condition for SetItemKeyOwner()
1530 ImGuiInputFlags_CondHovered = 1 << 22, // Only set if item is hovered (default to both)
1531 ImGuiInputFlags_CondActive = 1 << 23, // Only set if item is active (default to both)
1532 ImGuiInputFlags_CondDefault_ = ImGuiInputFlags_CondHovered | ImGuiInputFlags_CondActive,
1533
1534 // [Internal] Mask of which function support which flags
1535 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateMask_ = ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateDefault | ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateNavMove | ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateNavTweak,
1536 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilMask_ = ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilRelease | ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilKeyModsChange | ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilKeyModsChangeFromNone | ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilOtherKeyPress,
1537 ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatMask_ = ImGuiInputFlags_Repeat | ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatRateMask_ | ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatUntilMask_,
1538 ImGuiInputFlags_CondMask_ = ImGuiInputFlags_CondHovered | ImGuiInputFlags_CondActive,
1539 ImGuiInputFlags_RouteTypeMask_ = ImGuiInputFlags_RouteActive | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteFocused | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteGlobal | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteAlways,
1540 ImGuiInputFlags_RouteOptionsMask_ = ImGuiInputFlags_RouteOverFocused | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteOverActive | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteUnlessBgFocused | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteFromRootWindow,
1541 ImGuiInputFlags_SupportedByIsKeyPressed = ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatMask_,
1542 ImGuiInputFlags_SupportedByIsMouseClicked = ImGuiInputFlags_Repeat,
1543 ImGuiInputFlags_SupportedByShortcut = ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatMask_ | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteTypeMask_ | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteOptionsMask_,
1544 ImGuiInputFlags_SupportedBySetNextItemShortcut = ImGuiInputFlags_RepeatMask_ | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteTypeMask_ | ImGuiInputFlags_RouteOptionsMask_ | ImGuiInputFlags_Tooltip,
1545 ImGuiInputFlags_SupportedBySetKeyOwner = ImGuiInputFlags_LockThisFrame | ImGuiInputFlags_LockUntilRelease,
1546 ImGuiInputFlags_SupportedBySetItemKeyOwner = ImGuiInputFlags_SupportedBySetKeyOwner | ImGuiInputFlags_CondMask_,
1547};

1603 ImGuiScrollFlags_NoScrollParent = 1 << 6, // Disable forwarding scrolling to parent window if required to keep item/rect visible (only scroll window the function was applied to).

1818 bool IsKeyboardSetRange; // Set by BeginMultiSelect() when using Shift+Navigation. Because scrolling may be affected we can't afford a frame of lag with Shift+Navigation.

1820 bool RangeSrcPassedBy; // Set by the item that matches RangeSrcItem.

1851//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
1852// [SECTION] Viewport support
1853//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
1854
1855// ImGuiViewport Private/Internals fields (cardinal sin: we are using inheritance!)
1856// Every instance of ImGuiViewport is in fact a ImGuiViewportP.
1857struct ImGuiViewportP : public ImGuiViewport
1858{
1859 int BgFgDrawListsLastFrame[2]; // Last frame number the background (0) and foreground (1) draw lists were used
1860 ImDrawList* BgFgDrawLists[2]; // Convenience background (0) and foreground (1) draw lists. We use them to draw software mouser cursor when io.MouseDrawCursor is set and to draw most debug overlays.
1861 ImDrawData DrawDataP;
1862 ImDrawDataBuilder DrawDataBuilder; // Temporary data while building final ImDrawData
1863
1864 // Per-viewport work area
1865 // - Insets are >= 0.0f values, distance from viewport corners to work area.
1866 // - BeginMainMenuBar() and DockspaceOverViewport() tend to use work area to avoid stepping over existing contents.
1867 // - Generally 'safeAreaInsets' in iOS land, 'DisplayCutout' in Android land.
1868 ImVec2 WorkInsetMin; // Work Area inset locked for the frame. GetWorkRect() always fits within GetMainRect().
1869 ImVec2 WorkInsetMax; // "
1870 ImVec2 BuildWorkInsetMin; // Work Area inset accumulator for current frame, to become next frame's WorkInset
1871 ImVec2 BuildWorkInsetMax; // "
1872
1873 ImGuiViewportP() { BgFgDrawListsLastFrame[0] = BgFgDrawListsLastFrame[1] = -1; BgFgDrawLists[0] = BgFgDrawLists[1] = NULL; }
1874 ~ImGuiViewportP() { if (BgFgDrawLists[0]) IM_DELETE(BgFgDrawLists[0]); if (BgFgDrawLists[1]) IM_DELETE(BgFgDrawLists[1]); }
1875
1876 // Calculate work rect pos/size given a set of offset (we have 1 pair of offset for rect locked from last frame data, and 1 pair for currently building rect)
1877 ImVec2 CalcWorkRectPos(const ImVec2& inset_min) const { return ImVec2(Pos.x + inset_min.x, Pos.y + inset_min.y); }
1878 ImVec2 CalcWorkRectSize(const ImVec2& inset_min, const ImVec2& inset_max) const { return ImVec2(ImMax(0.0f, Size.x - inset_min.x - inset_max.x), ImMax(0.0f, Size.y - inset_min.y - inset_max.y)); }
1879 void UpdateWorkRect() { WorkPos = CalcWorkRectPos(WorkInsetMin); WorkSize = CalcWorkRectSize(WorkInsetMin, WorkInsetMax); } // Update public fields
1880
1881 // Helpers to retrieve ImRect (we don't need to store BuildWorkRect as every access tend to change it, hence the code asymmetry)
1882 ImRect GetMainRect() const { return ImRect(Pos.x, Pos.y, Pos.x + Size.x, Pos.y + Size.y); }
1883 ImRect GetWorkRect() const { return ImRect(WorkPos.x, WorkPos.y, WorkPos.x + WorkSize.x, WorkPos.y + WorkSize.y); }
1884 ImRect GetBuildWorkRect() const { ImVec2 pos = CalcWorkRectPos(BuildWorkInsetMin); ImVec2 size = CalcWorkRectSize(BuildWorkInsetMin, BuildWorkInsetMax); return ImRect(pos.x, pos.y, pos.x + size.x, pos.y + size.y); }
1885};

1949//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
1950// [SECTION] Error handling, State recovery support
1951//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
1952
1953// Macros used by Recoverable Error handling
1954// - Only dispatch error if _EXPR: evaluate as assert (similar to an assert macro).
1955// - The message will always be a string literal, in order to increase likelihood of being display by an assert handler.
1956// - See 'Demo->Configuration->Error Handling' and ImGuiIO definitions for details on error handling.
1957// - Read https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/wiki/Error-Handling for details on error handling.
1958#ifndef IM_ASSERT_USER_ERROR
1959#define IM_ASSERT_USER_ERROR(_EXPR,_MSG) do { if (!(_EXPR) && ImGui::ErrorLog(_MSG)) { IM_ASSERT((_EXPR) && _MSG); } } while (0) // Recoverable User Error
1960#endif
1961
1962// The error callback is currently not public, as it is expected that only advanced users will rely on it.
1963typedef void (*ImGuiErrorCallback)(ImGuiContext* ctx, void* user_data, const char* msg); // Function signature for g.ErrorCallback

2449 ImVec2 CursorPos; // Current emitting position, in absolute coordinates.
2450 ImVec2 CursorPosPrevLine;
2451 ImVec2 CursorStartPos; // Initial position after Begin(), generally ~ window position + WindowPadding.
2452 ImVec2 CursorMaxPos; // Used to implicitly calculate ContentSize at the beginning of next frame, for scrolling range and auto-resize. Always growing during the frame.
2453 ImVec2 IdealMaxPos; // Used to implicitly calculate ContentSizeIdeal at the beginning of next frame, for auto-resize only. Always growing during the frame.
2454 ImVec2 CurrLineSize;
2455 ImVec2 PrevLineSize;
2456 float CurrLineTextBaseOffset; // Baseline offset (0.0f by default on a new line, generally == style.FramePadding.y when a framed item has been added).
2457 float PrevLineTextBaseOffset;
2458 bool IsSameLine;
2459 bool IsSetPos;
2460 ImVec1 Indent; // Indentation / start position from left of window (increased by TreePush/TreePop, etc.)
2461 ImVec1 ColumnsOffset; // Offset to the current column (if ColumnsCurrent > 0). FIXME: This and the above should be a stack to allow use cases like Tree->Column->Tree. Need revamp columns API.
2462 ImVec1 GroupOffset;
2463 ImVec2 CursorStartPosLossyness;// Record the loss of precision of CursorStartPos due to really large scrolling amount. This is used by clipper to compensate and fix the most common use case of large scroll area.
2464
2465 // Keyboard/Gamepad navigation
2466 ImGuiNavLayer NavLayerCurrent; // Current layer, 0..31 (we currently only use 0..1)
2467 short NavLayersActiveMask; // Which layers have been written to (result from previous frame)
2468 short NavLayersActiveMaskNext;// Which layers have been written to (accumulator for current frame)
2469 bool NavIsScrollPushableX; // Set when current work location may be scrolled horizontally when moving left / right. This is generally always true UNLESS within a column.
2470 bool NavHideHighlightOneFrame;
2471 bool NavWindowHasScrollY; // Set per window when scrolling can be used (== ScrollMax.y > 0.0f)
2472
2473 // Miscellaneous
2474 bool MenuBarAppending; // FIXME: Remove this
2475 ImVec2 MenuBarOffset; // MenuBarOffset.x is sort of equivalent of a per-layer CursorPos.x, saved/restored as we switch to the menu bar. The only situation when MenuBarOffset.y is > 0 if when (SafeAreaPadding.y > FramePadding.y), often used on TVs.
2476 ImGuiMenuColumns MenuColumns; // Simplified columns storage for menu items measurement
2477 int TreeDepth; // Current tree depth.
2478 ImU32 TreeHasStackDataDepthMask; // Store whether given depth has ImGuiTreeNodeStackData data. Could be turned into a ImU64 if necessary.
2479 ImU32 TreeRecordsClippedNodesY2Mask; // Store whether we should keep recording Y2. Cleared when passing clip max. Equivalent TreeHasStackDataDepthMask value should always be set.
2480 ImVector<ImGuiWindow*> ChildWindows;
2481 ImGuiStorage* StateStorage; // Current persistent per-window storage (store e.g. tree node open/close state)
2482 ImGuiOldColumns* CurrentColumns; // Current columns set
2483 int CurrentTableIdx; // Current table index (into g.Tables)
2484 ImGuiLayoutType LayoutType;
2485 ImGuiLayoutType ParentLayoutType; // Layout type of parent window at the time of Begin()
2486 ImU32 ModalDimBgColor;
2487 ImGuiItemStatusFlags WindowItemStatusFlags;
2488 ImGuiItemStatusFlags ChildItemStatusFlags;
2489
2490 // Local parameters stacks
2491 // We store the current settings outside of the vectors to increase memory locality (reduce cache misses). The vectors are rarely modified. Also it allows us to not heap allocate for short-lived windows which are not using those settings.
2492 float ItemWidth; // Current item width (>0.0: width in pixels, <0.0: align xx pixels to the right of window).
2493 float TextWrapPos; // Current text wrap pos.
2494 ImVector<float> ItemWidthStack; // Store item widths to restore (attention: .back() is not == ItemWidth)
2495 ImVector<float> TextWrapPosStack; // Store text wrap pos to restore (attention: .back() is not == TextWrapPos)
2496};

2498// Storage for one window
2499struct IMGUI_API ImGuiWindow
2500{
2501 ImGuiContext* Ctx; // Parent UI context (needs to be set explicitly by parent).
2502 char* Name; // Window name, owned by the window.
2503 ImGuiID ID; // == ImHashStr(Name)
2504 ImGuiWindowFlags Flags; // See enum ImGuiWindowFlags_
2505 ImGuiChildFlags ChildFlags; // Set when window is a child window. See enum ImGuiChildFlags_
2506 ImGuiViewportP* Viewport; // Always set in Begin(). Inactive windows may have a NULL value here if their viewport was discarded.
2507 ImVec2 Pos; // Position (always rounded-up to nearest pixel)
2508 ImVec2 Size; // Current size (==SizeFull or collapsed title bar size)
2509 ImVec2 SizeFull; // Size when non collapsed
2510 ImVec2 ContentSize; // Size of contents/scrollable client area (calculated from the extents reach of the cursor) from previous frame. Does not include window decoration or window padding.
2511 ImVec2 ContentSizeIdeal;
2512 ImVec2 ContentSizeExplicit; // Size of contents/scrollable client area explicitly request by the user via SetNextWindowContentSize().
2513 ImVec2 WindowPadding; // Window padding at the time of Begin().
2514 float WindowRounding; // Window rounding at the time of Begin(). May be clamped lower to avoid rendering artifacts with title bar, menu bar etc.
2515 float WindowBorderSize; // Window border size at the time of Begin().
2516 float TitleBarHeight, MenuBarHeight; // Note that those used to be function before 2024/05/28. If you have old code calling TitleBarHeight() you can change it to TitleBarHeight.
2517 float DecoOuterSizeX1, DecoOuterSizeY1; // Left/Up offsets. Sum of non-scrolling outer decorations (X1 generally == 0.0f. Y1 generally = TitleBarHeight + MenuBarHeight). Locked during Begin().
2518 float DecoOuterSizeX2, DecoOuterSizeY2; // Right/Down offsets (X2 generally == ScrollbarSize.x, Y2 == ScrollbarSizes.y).
2519 float DecoInnerSizeX1, DecoInnerSizeY1; // Applied AFTER/OVER InnerRect. Specialized for Tables as they use specialized form of clipping and frozen rows/columns are inside InnerRect (and not part of regular decoration sizes).
2520 int NameBufLen; // Size of buffer storing Name. May be larger than strlen(Name)!
2521 ImGuiID MoveId; // == window->GetID("#MOVE")
2522 ImGuiID ChildId; // ID of corresponding item in parent window (for navigation to return from child window to parent window)
2523 ImGuiID PopupId; // ID in the popup stack when this window is used as a popup/menu (because we use generic Name/ID for recycling)
2524 ImVec2 Scroll;
2525 ImVec2 ScrollMax;
2526 ImVec2 ScrollTarget; // target scroll position. stored as cursor position with scrolling canceled out, so the highest point is always 0.0f. (FLT_MAX for no change)
2527 ImVec2 ScrollTargetCenterRatio; // 0.0f = scroll so that target position is at top, 0.5f = scroll so that target position is centered
2528 ImVec2 ScrollTargetEdgeSnapDist; // 0.0f = no snapping, >0.0f snapping threshold
2529 ImVec2 ScrollbarSizes; // Size taken by each scrollbars on their smaller axis. Pay attention! ScrollbarSizes.x == width of the vertical scrollbar, ScrollbarSizes.y = height of the horizontal scrollbar.
2530 bool ScrollbarX, ScrollbarY; // Are scrollbars visible?
2531 bool ScrollbarXStabilizeEnabled; // Was ScrollbarX previously auto-stabilized?
2532 ImU8 ScrollbarXStabilizeToggledHistory; // Used to stabilize scrollbar visibility in case of feedback loops
2533 bool Active; // Set to true on Begin(), unless Collapsed
2534 bool WasActive;
2535 bool WriteAccessed; // Set to true when any widget access the current window
2536 bool Collapsed; // Set when collapsing window to become only title-bar
2537 bool WantCollapseToggle;
2538 bool SkipItems; // Set when items can safely be all clipped (e.g. window not visible or collapsed)
2539 bool SkipRefresh; // [EXPERIMENTAL] Reuse previous frame drawn contents, Begin() returns false.
2540 bool Appearing; // Set during the frame where the window is appearing (or re-appearing)
2541 bool Hidden; // Do not display (== HiddenFrames*** > 0)
2542 bool IsFallbackWindow; // Set on the "Debug##Default" window.
2543 bool IsExplicitChild; // Set when passed _ChildWindow, left to false by BeginDocked()
2544 bool HasCloseButton; // Set when the window has a close button (p_open != NULL)
2545 signed char ResizeBorderHovered; // Current border being hovered for resize (-1: none, otherwise 0-3)
2546 signed char ResizeBorderHeld; // Current border being held for resize (-1: none, otherwise 0-3)
2547 short BeginCount; // Number of Begin() during the current frame (generally 0 or 1, 1+ if appending via multiple Begin/End pairs)
2548 short BeginCountPreviousFrame; // Number of Begin() during the previous frame
2549 short BeginOrderWithinParent; // Begin() order within immediate parent window, if we are a child window. Otherwise 0.
2550 short BeginOrderWithinContext; // Begin() order within entire imgui context. This is mostly used for debugging submission order related issues.
2551 short FocusOrder; // Order within WindowsFocusOrder[], altered when windows are focused.
2552 ImS8 AutoFitFramesX, AutoFitFramesY;
2553 bool AutoFitOnlyGrows;
2554 ImGuiDir AutoPosLastDirection;
2555 ImS8 HiddenFramesCanSkipItems; // Hide the window for N frames
2556 ImS8 HiddenFramesCannotSkipItems; // Hide the window for N frames while allowing items to be submitted so we can measure their size
2557 ImS8 HiddenFramesForRenderOnly; // Hide the window until frame N at Render() time only
2558 ImS8 DisableInputsFrames; // Disable window interactions for N frames
2559 ImGuiCond SetWindowPosAllowFlags : 8; // store acceptable condition flags for SetNextWindowPos() use.
2560 ImGuiCond SetWindowSizeAllowFlags : 8; // store acceptable condition flags for SetNextWindowSize() use.
2561 ImGuiCond SetWindowCollapsedAllowFlags : 8; // store acceptable condition flags for SetNextWindowCollapsed() use.
2562 ImVec2 SetWindowPosVal; // store window position when using a non-zero Pivot (position set needs to be processed when we know the window size)
2563 ImVec2 SetWindowPosPivot; // store window pivot for positioning. ImVec2(0, 0) when positioning from top-left corner; ImVec2(0.5f, 0.5f) for centering; ImVec2(1, 1) for bottom right.
2564
2565 ImVector<ImGuiID> IDStack; // ID stack. ID are hashes seeded with the value at the top of the stack. (In theory this should be in the TempData structure)
2566 ImGuiWindowTempData DC; // Temporary per-window data, reset at the beginning of the frame. This used to be called ImGuiDrawContext, hence the "DC" variable name.
2567
2568 // The best way to understand what those rectangles are is to use the 'Metrics->Tools->Show Windows Rectangles' viewer.
2569 // The main 'OuterRect', omitted as a field, is window->Rect().
2570 ImRect OuterRectClipped; // == Window->Rect() just after setup in Begin(). == window->Rect() for root window.
2571 ImRect InnerRect; // Inner rectangle (omit title bar, menu bar, scroll bar)
2572 ImRect InnerClipRect; // == InnerRect shrunk by WindowPadding*0.5f on each side, clipped within viewport or parent clip rect.
2573 ImRect WorkRect; // Initially covers the whole scrolling region. Reduced by containers e.g columns/tables when active. Shrunk by WindowPadding*1.0f on each side. This is meant to replace ContentRegionRect over time (from 1.71+ onward).
2574 ImRect ParentWorkRect; // Backup of WorkRect before entering a container such as columns/tables. Used by e.g. SpanAllColumns functions to easily access. Stacked containers are responsible for maintaining this. // FIXME-WORKRECT: Could be a stack?
2575 ImRect ClipRect; // Current clipping/scissoring rectangle, evolve as we are using PushClipRect(), etc. == DrawList->clip_rect_stack.back().
2576 ImRect ContentRegionRect; // FIXME: This is currently confusing/misleading. It is essentially WorkRect but not handling of scrolling. We currently rely on it as right/bottom aligned sizing operation need some size to rely on.
2577 ImVec2ih HitTestHoleSize; // Define an optional rectangular hole where mouse will pass-through the window.
2578 ImVec2ih HitTestHoleOffset;
2579
2580 int LastFrameActive; // Last frame number the window was Active.
2581 float LastTimeActive; // Last timestamp the window was Active (using float as we don't need high precision there)
2582 float ItemWidthDefault;
2583 ImGuiStorage StateStorage;
2584 ImVector<ImGuiOldColumns> ColumnsStorage;
2585 float FontWindowScale; // User scale multiplier per-window, via SetWindowFontScale()
2586 float FontWindowScaleParents;
2587 float FontRefSize; // This is a copy of window->CalcFontSize() at the time of Begin(), trying to phase out CalcFontSize() especially as it may be called on non-current window.
2588 int SettingsOffset; // Offset into SettingsWindows[] (offsets are always valid as we only grow the array from the back)
2589
2590 ImDrawList* DrawList; // == &DrawListInst (for backward compatibility reason with code using imgui_internal.h we keep this a pointer)
2591 ImDrawList DrawListInst;
2592 ImGuiWindow* ParentWindow; // If we are a child _or_ popup _or_ docked window, this is pointing to our parent. Otherwise NULL.
2593 ImGuiWindow* ParentWindowInBeginStack;
2594 ImGuiWindow* RootWindow; // Point to ourself or first ancestor that is not a child window. Doesn't cross through popups/dock nodes.
2595 ImGuiWindow* RootWindowPopupTree; // Point to ourself or first ancestor that is not a child window. Cross through popups parent<>child.
2596 ImGuiWindow* RootWindowForTitleBarHighlight; // Point to ourself or first ancestor which will display TitleBgActive color when this window is active.
2597 ImGuiWindow* RootWindowForNav; // Point to ourself or first ancestor which doesn't have the NavFlattened flag.
2598 ImGuiWindow* ParentWindowForFocusRoute; // Set to manual link a window to its logical parent so that Shortcut() chain are honoerd (e.g. Tool linked to Document)
2599
2600 ImGuiWindow* NavLastChildNavWindow; // When going to the menu bar, we remember the child window we came from. (This could probably be made implicit if we kept g.Windows sorted by last focused including child window.)
2601 ImGuiID NavLastIds[ImGuiNavLayer_COUNT]; // Last known NavId for this window, per layer (0/1)
2602 ImRect NavRectRel[ImGuiNavLayer_COUNT]; // Reference rectangle, in window relative space
2603 ImVec2 NavPreferredScoringPosRel[ImGuiNavLayer_COUNT]; // Preferred X/Y position updated when moving on a given axis, reset to FLT_MAX.
2604 ImGuiID NavRootFocusScopeId; // Focus Scope ID at the time of Begin()
2605
2606 int MemoryDrawListIdxCapacity; // Backup of last idx/vtx count, so when waking up the window we can preallocate and avoid iterative alloc/copy
2607 int MemoryDrawListVtxCapacity;
2608 bool MemoryCompacted; // Set when window extraneous data have been garbage collected
2609
2610public:
2611 ImGuiWindow(ImGuiContext* context, const char* name);
2612 ~ImGuiWindow();
2613
2614 ImGuiID GetID(const char* str, const char* str_end = NULL);
2615 ImGuiID GetID(const void* ptr);
2616 ImGuiID GetID(int n);
2617 ImGuiID GetIDFromPos(const ImVec2& p_abs);
2618 ImGuiID GetIDFromRectangle(const ImRect& r_abs);
2619
2620 // We don't use g.FontSize because the window may be != g.CurrentWindow.
2621 ImRect Rect() const { return ImRect(Pos.x, Pos.y, Pos.x + Size.x, Pos.y + Size.y); }
2622 float CalcFontSize() const { ImGuiContext& g = *Ctx; return g.FontBaseSize * FontWindowScale * FontWindowScaleParents; }
2623 ImRect TitleBarRect() const { return ImRect(Pos, ImVec2(Pos.x + SizeFull.x, Pos.y + TitleBarHeight)); }
2624 ImRect MenuBarRect() const { float y1 = Pos.y + TitleBarHeight; return ImRect(Pos.x, y1, Pos.x + SizeFull.x, y1 + MenuBarHeight); }
2625};

2664
2665 ImGuiTabItem() { memset(this, 0, sizeof(*this)); LastFrameVisible = LastFrameSelected = -1; RequestedWidth = -1.0f; NameOffset = -1; BeginOrder = IndexDuringLayout = -1; }

2709//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
2710// [SECTION] Table support
2711//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
2712
2713#define IM_COL32_DISABLE IM_COL32(0,0,0,1) // Special sentinel code which cannot be used as a regular color.
2714#define IMGUI_TABLE_MAX_COLUMNS 512 // Arbitrary "safety" maximum, may be lifted in the future if needed. Must fit in ImGuiTableColumnIdx/ImGuiTableDrawChannelIdx.
2715
2716// [Internal] sizeof() ~ 112
2717// We use the terminology "Enabled" to refer to a column that is not Hidden by user/api.
2718// We use the terminology "Clipped" to refer to a column that is out of sight because of scrolling/clipping.
2719// This is in contrast with some user-facing api such as IsItemVisible() / IsRectVisible() which use "Visible" to mean "not clipped".
2720struct ImGuiTableColumn
2721{
2722 ImGuiTableColumnFlags Flags; // Flags after some patching (not directly same as provided by user). See ImGuiTableColumnFlags_
2723 float WidthGiven; // Final/actual width visible == (MaxX - MinX), locked in TableUpdateLayout(). May be > WidthRequest to honor minimum width, may be < WidthRequest to honor shrinking columns down in tight space.
2724 float MinX; // Absolute positions
2725 float MaxX;
2726 float WidthRequest; // Master width absolute value when !(Flags & _WidthStretch). When Stretch this is derived every frame from StretchWeight in TableUpdateLayout()
2727 float WidthAuto; // Automatic width
2728 float WidthMax; // Maximum width (FIXME: overwritten by each instance)
2729 float StretchWeight; // Master width weight when (Flags & _WidthStretch). Often around ~1.0f initially.
2730 float InitStretchWeightOrWidth; // Value passed to TableSetupColumn(). For Width it is a content width (_without padding_).
2731 ImRect ClipRect; // Clipping rectangle for the column
2732 ImGuiID UserID; // Optional, value passed to TableSetupColumn()
2733 float WorkMinX; // Contents region min ~(MinX + CellPaddingX + CellSpacingX1) == cursor start position when entering column
2734 float WorkMaxX; // Contents region max ~(MaxX - CellPaddingX - CellSpacingX2)
2735 float ItemWidth; // Current item width for the column, preserved across rows
2736 float ContentMaxXFrozen; // Contents maximum position for frozen rows (apart from headers), from which we can infer content width.
2737 float ContentMaxXUnfrozen;
2738 float ContentMaxXHeadersUsed; // Contents maximum position for headers rows (regardless of freezing). TableHeader() automatically softclip itself + report ideal desired size, to avoid creating extraneous draw calls
2739 float ContentMaxXHeadersIdeal;
2740 ImS16 NameOffset; // Offset into parent ColumnsNames[]
2741 ImGuiTableColumnIdx DisplayOrder; // Index within Table's IndexToDisplayOrder[] (column may be reordered by users)
2742 ImGuiTableColumnIdx IndexWithinEnabledSet; // Index within enabled/visible set (<= IndexToDisplayOrder)
2743 ImGuiTableColumnIdx PrevEnabledColumn; // Index of prev enabled/visible column within Columns[], -1 if first enabled/visible column
2744 ImGuiTableColumnIdx NextEnabledColumn; // Index of next enabled/visible column within Columns[], -1 if last enabled/visible column
2745 ImGuiTableColumnIdx SortOrder; // Index of this column within sort specs, -1 if not sorting on this column, 0 for single-sort, may be >0 on multi-sort
2746 ImGuiTableDrawChannelIdx DrawChannelCurrent; // Index within DrawSplitter.Channels[]
2747 ImGuiTableDrawChannelIdx DrawChannelFrozen; // Draw channels for frozen rows (often headers)
2748 ImGuiTableDrawChannelIdx DrawChannelUnfrozen; // Draw channels for unfrozen rows
2749 bool IsEnabled; // IsUserEnabled && (Flags & ImGuiTableColumnFlags_Disabled) == 0
2750 bool IsUserEnabled; // Is the column not marked Hidden by the user? (unrelated to being off view, e.g. clipped by scrolling).
2751 bool IsUserEnabledNextFrame;
2752 bool IsVisibleX; // Is actually in view (e.g. overlapping the host window clipping rectangle, not scrolled).
2753 bool IsVisibleY;
2754 bool IsRequestOutput; // Return value for TableSetColumnIndex() / TableNextColumn(): whether we request user to output contents or not.
2755 bool IsSkipItems; // Do we want item submissions to this column to be completely ignored (no layout will happen).
2756 bool IsPreserveWidthAuto;
2757 ImS8 NavLayerCurrent; // ImGuiNavLayer in 1 byte
2758 ImU8 AutoFitQueue; // Queue of 8 values for the next 8 frames to request auto-fit
2759 ImU8 CannotSkipItemsQueue; // Queue of 8 values for the next 8 frames to disable Clipped/SkipItem
2760 ImU8 SortDirection : 2; // ImGuiSortDirection_Ascending or ImGuiSortDirection_Descending
2761 ImU8 SortDirectionsAvailCount : 2; // Number of available sort directions (0 to 3)
2762 ImU8 SortDirectionsAvailMask : 4; // Mask of available sort directions (1-bit each)
2763 ImU8 SortDirectionsAvailList; // Ordered list of available sort directions (2-bits each, total 8-bits)
2764
2765 ImGuiTableColumn()
2766 {
2767 memset(this, 0, sizeof(*this));
2768 StretchWeight = WidthRequest = -1.0f;
2769 NameOffset = -1;
2770 DisplayOrder = IndexWithinEnabledSet = -1;
2771 PrevEnabledColumn = NextEnabledColumn = -1;
2772 SortOrder = -1;
2773 SortDirection = ImGuiSortDirection_None;
2774 DrawChannelCurrent = DrawChannelFrozen = DrawChannelUnfrozen = (ImU8)-1;
2775 }
2776};
2777
2778// Transient cell data stored per row.
2779// sizeof() ~ 6 bytes
2780struct ImGuiTableCellData
2781{
2782 ImU32 BgColor; // Actual color
2783 ImGuiTableColumnIdx Column; // Column number
2784};
2785
2786// Parameters for TableAngledHeadersRowEx()
2787// This may end up being refactored for more general purpose.
2788// sizeof() ~ 12 bytes
2789struct ImGuiTableHeaderData
2790{
2791 ImGuiTableColumnIdx Index; // Column index
2792 ImU32 TextColor;
2793 ImU32 BgColor0;
2794 ImU32 BgColor1;
2795};

2797// Per-instance data that needs preserving across frames (seemingly most others do not need to be preserved aside from debug needs. Does that means they could be moved to ImGuiTableTempData?)
2798// sizeof() ~ 24 bytes
2799struct ImGuiTableInstanceData
2800{
2801 ImGuiID TableInstanceID;
2802 float LastOuterHeight; // Outer height from last frame
2803 float LastTopHeadersRowHeight; // Height of first consecutive header rows from last frame (FIXME: this is used assuming consecutive headers are in same frozen set)
2804 float LastFrozenHeight; // Height of frozen section from last frame
2805 int HoveredRowLast; // Index of row which was hovered last frame.
2806 int HoveredRowNext; // Index of row hovered this frame, set after encountering it.
2807
2808 ImGuiTableInstanceData() { TableInstanceID = 0; LastOuterHeight = LastTopHeadersRowHeight = LastFrozenHeight = 0.0f; HoveredRowLast = HoveredRowNext = -1; }
2809};
2810
2811// sizeof() ~ 592 bytes + heap allocs described in TableBeginInitMemory()
2812struct IMGUI_API ImGuiTable
2813{
2814 ImGuiID ID;
2815 ImGuiTableFlags Flags;
2816 void* RawData; // Single allocation to hold Columns[], DisplayOrderToIndex[], and RowCellData[]
2817 ImGuiTableTempData* TempData; // Transient data while table is active. Point within g.CurrentTableStack[]
2818 ImSpan<ImGuiTableColumn> Columns; // Point within RawData[]
2819 ImSpan<ImGuiTableColumnIdx> DisplayOrderToIndex; // Point within RawData[]. Store display order of columns (when not reordered, the values are 0...Count-1)
2820 ImSpan<ImGuiTableCellData> RowCellData; // Point within RawData[]. Store cells background requests for current row.
2821 ImBitArrayPtr EnabledMaskByDisplayOrder; // Column DisplayOrder -> IsEnabled map
2822 ImBitArrayPtr EnabledMaskByIndex; // Column Index -> IsEnabled map (== not hidden by user/api) in a format adequate for iterating column without touching cold data
2823 ImBitArrayPtr VisibleMaskByIndex; // Column Index -> IsVisibleX|IsVisibleY map (== not hidden by user/api && not hidden by scrolling/cliprect)
2824 ImGuiTableFlags SettingsLoadedFlags; // Which data were loaded from the .ini file (e.g. when order is not altered we won't save order)
2825 int SettingsOffset; // Offset in g.SettingsTables
2826 int LastFrameActive;
2827 int ColumnsCount; // Number of columns declared in BeginTable()
2828 int CurrentRow;

2843 ImU32 BorderColorLight;

2845 float BorderX2;

2852 float InnerWidth; // User value passed to BeginTable(), see comments at the top of BeginTable() for details.
2853 float ColumnsGivenWidth; // Sum of current column width
2854 float ColumnsAutoFitWidth; // Sum of ideal column width in order nothing to be clipped, used for auto-fitting and content width submission in outer window
2855 float ColumnsStretchSumWeights; // Sum of weight of all enabled stretching columns
2856 float ResizedColumnNextWidth;

2860 float AngledHeadersSlope; // Set by TableAngledHeadersRow(), used in TableUpdateLayout()
2861 ImRect OuterRect; // Note: for non-scrolling table, OuterRect.Max.y is often FLT_MAX until EndTable(), unless a height has been specified in BeginTable().

2877 ImVector<ImGuiTableColumnSortSpecs> SortSpecsMulti; // FIXME-OPT: Using a small-vector pattern would be good.

2883 ImGuiTableColumnIdx AngledHeadersCount; // Count columns with angled headers

2907 bool IsLayoutLocked; // Set by TableUpdateLayout() which is called when beginning the first row.
2908 bool IsInsideRow; // Set when inside TableBeginRow()/TableEndRow().

2911 bool IsUsingHeaders; // Set when the first row had the ImGuiTableRowFlags_Headers flag.

2914 bool IsSettingsRequestLoad;

2916 bool IsDefaultDisplayOrder; // Set when display order is unchanged from default (DisplayOrder contains 0...Count-1)
2917 bool IsResetAllRequest;
2918 bool IsResetDisplayOrderRequest;
2919 bool IsUnfrozenRows; // Set when we got past the frozen row.
2920 bool IsDefaultSizingPolicy; // Set if user didn't explicitly set a sizing policy in BeginTable()
2921 bool IsActiveIdAliveBeforeTable;
2922 bool IsActiveIdInTable;
2923 bool HasScrollbarYCurr; // Whether ANY instance of this table had a vertical scrollbar during the current frame.
2924 bool HasScrollbarYPrev; // Whether ANY instance of this table had a vertical scrollbar during the previous.
2925 bool MemoryCompacted;

2928 ImGuiTable() { memset(this, 0, sizeof(*this)); LastFrameActive = -1; }
2929 ~ImGuiTable() { IM_FREE(RawData); }

2932// Transient data that are only needed between BeginTable() and EndTable(), those buffers are shared (1 per level of stacked table).
2933// - Accessing those requires chasing an extra pointer so for very frequently used data we leave them in the main table structure.
2934// - We also leave out of this structure data that tend to be particularly useful for debugging/metrics.
2935// FIXME-TABLE: more transient data could be stored in a stacked ImGuiTableTempData: e.g. SortSpecs.
2936// sizeof() ~ 136 bytes.
2937struct IMGUI_API ImGuiTableTempData
2938{
2939 int TableIndex; // Index in g.Tables.Buf[] pool
2940 float LastTimeActive; // Last timestamp this structure was used
2941 float AngledHeadersExtraWidth; // Used in EndTable()
2942 ImVector<ImGuiTableHeaderData> AngledHeadersRequests; // Used in TableAngledHeadersRow()
2943
2944 ImVec2 UserOuterSize; // outer_size.x passed to BeginTable()
2945 ImDrawListSplitter DrawSplitter;
2946
2947 ImRect HostBackupWorkRect; // Backup of InnerWindow->WorkRect at the end of BeginTable()
2948 ImRect HostBackupParentWorkRect; // Backup of InnerWindow->ParentWorkRect at the end of BeginTable()
2949 ImVec2 HostBackupPrevLineSize; // Backup of InnerWindow->DC.PrevLineSize at the end of BeginTable()
2950 ImVec2 HostBackupCurrLineSize; // Backup of InnerWindow->DC.CurrLineSize at the end of BeginTable()
2951 ImVec2 HostBackupCursorMaxPos; // Backup of InnerWindow->DC.CursorMaxPos at the end of BeginTable()
2952 ImVec1 HostBackupColumnsOffset; // Backup of OuterWindow->DC.ColumnsOffset at the end of BeginTable()
2953 float HostBackupItemWidth; // Backup of OuterWindow->DC.ItemWidth at the end of BeginTable()
2954 int HostBackupItemWidthStackSize;//Backup of OuterWindow->DC.ItemWidthStack.Size at the end of BeginTable()
2955
2956 ImGuiTableTempData() { memset(this, 0, sizeof(*this)); LastTimeActive = -1.0f; }
2957};

2983// This is designed to be stored in a single ImChunkStream (1 header followed by N ImGuiTableColumnSettings, etc.)
2984struct ImGuiTableSettings
2985{
2986 ImGuiID ID; // Set to 0 to invalidate/delete the setting
2987 ImGuiTableFlags SaveFlags; // Indicate data we want to save using the Resizable/Reorderable/Sortable/Hideable flags (could be using its own flags..)
2988 float RefScale; // Reference scale to be able to rescale columns on font/dpi changes.
2989 ImGuiTableColumnIdx ColumnsCount;
2990 ImGuiTableColumnIdx ColumnsCountMax; // Maximum number of columns this settings instance can store, we can recycle a settings instance with lower number of columns but not higher
2991 bool WantApply; // Set when loaded from .ini data (to enable merging/loading .ini data into an already running context)
2992
2993 ImGuiTableSettings() { memset(this, 0, sizeof(*this)); }
2994 ImGuiTableColumnSettings* GetColumnSettings() { return (ImGuiTableColumnSettings*)(this + 1); }
2995};

3238 // [EXPERIMENTAL] Low-Level: Key/Input Ownership
3239 // - The idea is that instead of "eating" a given input, we can link to an owner id.
3240 // - Ownership is most often claimed as a result of reacting to a press/down event (but occasionally may be claimed ahead).
3241 // - Input queries can then read input by specifying ImGuiKeyOwner_Any (== 0), ImGuiKeyOwner_NoOwner (== -1) or a custom ID.
3242 // - Legacy input queries (without specifying an owner or _Any or _None) are equivalent to using ImGuiKeyOwner_Any (== 0).
3243 // - Input ownership is automatically released on the frame after a key is released. Therefore:
3244 // - for ownership registration happening as a result of a down/press event, the SetKeyOwner() call may be done once (common case).
3245 // - for ownership registration happening ahead of a down/press event, the SetKeyOwner() call needs to be made every frame (happens if e.g. claiming ownership on hover).
3246 // - SetItemKeyOwner() is a shortcut for common simple case. A custom widget will probably want to call SetKeyOwner() multiple times directly based on its interaction state.
3247 // - This is marked experimental because not all widgets are fully honoring the Set/Test idioms. We will need to move forward step by step.
3248 // Please open a GitHub Issue to submit your usage scenario or if there's a use case you need solved.
3249 IMGUI_API ImGuiID GetKeyOwner(ImGuiKey key);
3250 IMGUI_API void SetKeyOwner(ImGuiKey key, ImGuiID owner_id, ImGuiInputFlags flags = 0);
3251 IMGUI_API void SetKeyOwnersForKeyChord(ImGuiKeyChord key, ImGuiID owner_id, ImGuiInputFlags flags = 0);
3252 IMGUI_API void SetItemKeyOwner(ImGuiKey key, ImGuiInputFlags flags); // Set key owner to last item if it is hovered or active. Equivalent to 'if (IsItemHovered() || IsItemActive()) { SetKeyOwner(key, GetItemID());'.
3253 IMGUI_API bool TestKeyOwner(ImGuiKey key, ImGuiID owner_id); // Test that key is either not owned, either owned by 'owner_id'
3254 inline ImGuiKeyOwnerData* GetKeyOwnerData(ImGuiContext* ctx, ImGuiKey key) { if (key & ImGuiMod_Mask_) key = ConvertSingleModFlagToKey(key); IM_ASSERT(IsNamedKey(key)); return &ctx->KeysOwnerData[key - ImGuiKey_NamedKey_BEGIN]; }
3255
3256 // [EXPERIMENTAL] High-Level: Input Access functions w/ support for Key/Input Ownership
3257 // - Important: legacy IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey, bool repeat=true) _DEFAULTS_ to repeat, new IsKeyPressed() requires _EXPLICIT_ ImGuiInputFlags_Repeat flag.
3258 // - Expected to be later promoted to public API, the prototypes are designed to replace existing ones (since owner_id can default to Any == 0)
3259 // - Specifying a value for 'ImGuiID owner' will test that EITHER the key is NOT owned (UNLESS locked), EITHER the key is owned by 'owner'.
3260 // Legacy functions use ImGuiKeyOwner_Any meaning that they typically ignore ownership, unless a call to SetKeyOwner() explicitly used ImGuiInputFlags_LockThisFrame or ImGuiInputFlags_LockUntilRelease.
3261 // - Binding generators may want to ignore those for now, or suffix them with Ex() until we decide if this gets moved into public API.
3262 IMGUI_API bool IsKeyDown(ImGuiKey key, ImGuiID owner_id);
3263 IMGUI_API bool IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey key, ImGuiInputFlags flags, ImGuiID owner_id = 0); // Important: when transitioning from old to new IsKeyPressed(): old API has "bool repeat = true", so would default to repeat. New API requiress explicit ImGuiInputFlags_Repeat.
3264 IMGUI_API bool IsKeyReleased(ImGuiKey key, ImGuiID owner_id);
3265 IMGUI_API bool IsKeyChordPressed(ImGuiKeyChord key_chord, ImGuiInputFlags flags, ImGuiID owner_id = 0);
3266 IMGUI_API bool IsMouseDown(ImGuiMouseButton button, ImGuiID owner_id);
3267 IMGUI_API bool IsMouseClicked(ImGuiMouseButton button, ImGuiInputFlags flags, ImGuiID owner_id = 0);
3268 IMGUI_API bool IsMouseReleased(ImGuiMouseButton button, ImGuiID owner_id);
3269 IMGUI_API bool IsMouseDoubleClicked(ImGuiMouseButton button, ImGuiID owner_id);

3271 // Shortcut Testing & Routing
3272 // - Set Shortcut() and SetNextItemShortcut() in imgui.h
3273 // - When a policy (except for ImGuiInputFlags_RouteAlways *) is set, Shortcut() will register itself with SetShortcutRouting(),
3274 // allowing the system to decide where to route the input among other route-aware calls.
3275 // (* using ImGuiInputFlags_RouteAlways is roughly equivalent to calling IsKeyChordPressed(key) and bypassing route registration and check)
3276 // - When using one of the routing option:
3277 // - The default route is ImGuiInputFlags_RouteFocused (accept inputs if window is in focus stack. Deep-most focused window takes inputs. ActiveId takes inputs over deep-most focused window.)
3278 // - Routes are requested given a chord (key + modifiers) and a routing policy.
3279 // - Routes are resolved during NewFrame(): if keyboard modifiers are matching current ones: SetKeyOwner() is called + route is granted for the frame.
3280 // - Each route may be granted to a single owner. When multiple requests are made we have policies to select the winning route (e.g. deep most window).
3281 // - Multiple read sites may use the same owner id can all access the granted route.
3282 // - When owner_id is 0 we use the current Focus Scope ID as a owner ID in order to identify our location.
3283 // - You can chain two unrelated windows in the focus stack using SetWindowParentWindowForFocusRoute()
3284 // e.g. if you have a tool window associated to a document, and you want document shortcuts to run when the tool is focused.
3285 IMGUI_API bool Shortcut(ImGuiKeyChord key_chord, ImGuiInputFlags flags, ImGuiID owner_id);
3286 IMGUI_API bool SetShortcutRouting(ImGuiKeyChord key_chord, ImGuiInputFlags flags, ImGuiID owner_id); // owner_id needs to be explicit and cannot be 0
3287 IMGUI_API bool TestShortcutRouting(ImGuiKeyChord key_chord, ImGuiID owner_id);
3288 IMGUI_API ImGuiKeyRoutingData* GetShortcutRoutingData(ImGuiKeyChord key_chord);

3290 // [EXPERIMENTAL] Focus Scope
3291 // This is generally used to identify a unique input location (for e.g. a selection set)
3292 // There is one per window (automatically set in Begin), but:
3293 // - Selection patterns generally need to react (e.g. clear a selection) when landing on one item of the set.
3294 // So in order to identify a set multiple lists in same window may each need a focus scope.
3295 // If you imagine an hypothetical BeginSelectionGroup()/EndSelectionGroup() api, it would likely call PushFocusScope()/EndFocusScope()
3296 // - Shortcut routing also use focus scope as a default location identifier if an owner is not provided.
3297 // We don't use the ID Stack for this as it is common to want them separate.
3298 IMGUI_API void PushFocusScope(ImGuiID id);
3299 IMGUI_API void PopFocusScope();
3300 inline ImGuiID GetCurrentFocusScope() { ImGuiContext& g = *GImGui; return g.CurrentFocusScopeId; } // Focus scope we are outputting into, set by PushFocusScope()

3585 // (Old) IMGUI_VERSION_NUM >= 18209: using 'ItemAdd(..., ImGuiItemAddFlags_Focusable)' and 'bool tab_focused = (g.LastItemData.StatusFlags & ImGuiItemStatusFlags_Focused) != 0'
3586 // (New) IMGUI_VERSION_NUM >= 18413: using 'ItemAdd(..., ImGuiItemFlags_Inputable)' and 'bool tab_focused = (g.NavActivateId == id && (g.NavActivateFlags & ImGuiActivateFlags_PreferInput))'
3587 //inline bool FocusableItemRegister(ImGuiWindow* window, ImGuiID id) // -> pass ImGuiItemAddFlags_Inputable flag to ItemAdd()
3588 //inline void FocusableItemUnregister(ImGuiWindow* window) // -> unnecessary: TempInputText() uses ImGuiInputTextFlags_MergedItem
